blocks.text: Someone was mocking the little owl. She, however, parried each of the jibes with clever speech. Obj. What a head! Resp. But what sort of head does Jupiter have? Obj. And the grey-blue colour? Resp. This is proper to Minerva, the goddess with grey-blue eyes. Obj. You sing unpleasantly. Resp. The magpie sings even more unpleasantly. Obj. How (supply will it be excused) the thinness of your foot? Resp. What do you think of the starling? But after she had easily refuted everything, she was beaten on one point, however wise she was. Obj. But, as a wise one, take note: each of these is found singly in each of them, but in you all of them together, and beyond measure; for you are grey-blue, and crude in song, and thin of foot [col. 292] [III, 39], and heavy of head. At these words the good little owl went away, covered with shame ^{(5)}.
